audits.title: 144 Title: A Repeat Cycle Closed Loop Audit Reviewing Emergency Department Referrals for Nasal Trauma to a Major ENT Centre; Practice Standards for Safe Care
audits.standard: Assessment and documentation of septal haematoma, infraorbital nerve status and airflow symptoms
audits.setting: Emergency department referrals to a major ENT centre emergency clinic, Imperial College Healthcare Trust
audits.intervention: Presentation at ED teaching and board rounds, then a new trust guideline uploaded to the ED guidance app.

cycle2.result: Septal haematoma 85%; airflow symptoms 33%; infraorbital nerve reviewed in 5% more patients.

audits.other_findings: Three cycles with 137 patients in total; referrals were 26% higher before the first intervention.
audits.citation: Kennard B, Bickerton R, Parker-Conway K. 144 Title: A Repeat Cycle Closed Loop Audit Reviewing Emergency Department Referrals for Nasal Trauma to a Major ENT Centre; Practice Standards for Safe Care. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.389.

audits.title: 256 Straight to the Point: Improving Nasal Fracture Care Through a Face-to-Face-First Pathway - a Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: ENT UK standard: manipulation within 21 days

cycle1.result: Telemedicine-first pathway: mean time to face-to-face review 16.5 days; mean time to MUA 15.2 days; MUA within 14 days 38.9%; 1.23 consultations per patient.

audits.intervention: Change from a telemedicine-first to a face-to-face-first pathway.

cycle2.result: Mean time to face-to-face review 13.3 days (p=0.0068); mean time to MUA 13.9 days (p=0.19) with 100% within 21 days; MUA within 14 days 57.1%; 1.04 consultations per patient.

audits.other_findings: Discharge from ENT earlier (15.2 to 12.2 days, p=0.0019); MUA patients were younger (mean 31.3 vs 41.7 years).
audits.citation: Mao E, Bawa J, Abdul-Hamid A. 256 Straight to the Point: Improving Nasal Fracture Care Through a Face-to-Face-First Pathway - a Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.209.

audits.title: Audit of nasal fracture management in accident and emergency in a district general hospital.
audits.standard: Best practice for nasal fracture management
audits.setting: Accident and emergency department of a busy district general hospital

cycle1.result: 10 had nasal X-ray; 9 had no documentation of septal haematoma; 7 had no follow-up arranged.

audits.intervention: Education and a departmental protocol based on best practice.

cycle2.result: Two nasal X-rays (looking for foreign bodies); all patients had septal haematoma documentation and appropriate follow-up.

audits.citation: Agrawal N, Brayley N. Audit of nasal fracture management in accident and emergency in a district general hospital. J Eval Clin Pract. 2007;13(2):295-297. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2753.2006.00700.x. PMID: 17378878.

audits.title: Nasal injury management: an audit of accident and emergency practice.
audits.standard: Local nasal injury management guideline (refer only patients with deformity after swelling subsides)
audits.setting: ENT outpatients receiving A&E nasal injury referrals, University Hospital of North Staffordshire

cycle1.result: Nasal injury referrals seen in ENT outpatients before the guideline, including those not requiring ENT treatment (figures not reported in abstract).

audits.intervention: Introduction of a nasal injury management guideline for A&E

cycle2.result: Proportion of patients seen in ENT outpatients not requiring any ENT treatment was reduced (figures not reported in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Authors suggest the guideline may also prevent delayed ENT input for new onset nasal deformity.
audits.citation: Grainger J, George A, Coulson C, De R. Nasal injury management: an audit of accident and emergency practice. Eur Arch Otorhinolaryngol. 2009;266(12):1995-1999. doi:10.1007/s00405-009-0964-1. PMID: 19340445.

audits.title: Audit of Nasal Bone Fracture Referrals to an ENT Hub: Timeliness of Review and Management.
audits.standard: ENT UK and BAOMS guidance: patients requiring reduction of nasal bone fractures assessed and managed within 7–14 days of injury.
audits.setting: ENT hub (email referrals with telephone triage and rapid access clinic), Ulster Hospital, Dundonald, Belfast Health and Social Care Trust

cycle1.result: 93% (52/56) referred within 7 days of injury; 63% (35/56) contacted within 7 days of referral; 74% (25/34) seen in clinic within two weeks of injury (82% in abstract); 68% (13/19) had manipulation within 14 days.

audits.other_findings: Telephone triage avoided clinic attendance for 39% (22/56). All three paediatric patients needing manipulation under general anaesthetic exceeded 14 days due to theatre capacity.
audits.citation: McAdam J. Audit of Nasal Bone Fracture Referrals to an ENT Hub: Timeliness of Review and Management. Cureus. 2025;17(9):e92814. doi:10.7759/cureus.92814. PMID: 41127738.
